title: Quantum causal correlations conjecture for chordless siblings-on-cycles graphs
statement: Let $W$ be a quantum process with causal structure $G=(V,E)$. A process produces causal correlations when, for every collection of local experiments $\mu$, the resulting correlations $p(a\mid x)$ are causal. **Quantum causal correlations conjecture.** If $G$ is a chordless siblings-on-cycles graph, then $W$ always produces causal correlations. The corresponding statement is proved for classical-deterministic processes by reducing successively at source nodes. Whether every quantum process on a chordless siblings-on-cycles graph produces only causal correlations remains open.
source_name: Eleftherios-Ermis Tselentis and Ämin Baumeler, “Admissible Causal Structures and Correlations”, arXiv:2210.12796 (2023).
references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2021–2022). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2108.12209](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12209).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2210.12796

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of October 2022).
